name: Denial of Service
summary: Adversaries may perform Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks to disrupt expected device functionality. Examples of DoS attacks include overwhelming the target device with a high volume of requests in a short time period and sending the target device a request it does not know how to handle. Disrupting device state may temporarily render it unresponsive, possibly lasting until a reboot can occur. When placed in this state, devices may be unable to…

analytics.name: Analytic 1856
analytics.guidance: Real-time network monitoring identifies a sustained spike in malformed or high-volume Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol traffic directed at a single field device from a source not in the approved control server list, immediately followed by that device dropping out of the supervisory poll cycle. Documented precedent: Sandworm's Industroyer malware sent a crafted 18-byte proprietary User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet to port 50000 on Siemens Protection Technology (SIPROTEC) relays (CVE-2015-5374), causing the device to hang and require a manual reboot. analytics.name: Analytic 2121
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux service process (historian daemon, Open Platform Communications (OPC) gateway) being killed or crashing following a sustained high-rate inbound connection pattern recorded by network monitoring, correlated with daemon log entries indicating connection limit exhaustion or out-of-memory conditions. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when a device-specific traffic/resource threshold is exceeded and the same window shows service degradation, failed polling, device alarm/restart, resource exhaustion, or malformed/out-of-spec protocol behavior.
